analysis.title: BofA on USA: Weekly spending update through Oct 31
key_insights: Total card spending per household rose 6.2% y/y in the week ending Oct 31, based on BAC aggregated credit and debit card data (7-day moving average, y/y).
Total card spending excluding gas rose 5.1% y/y on Oct 31. Gas spending ran +25.0% y/y, which lifts the headline figure by about 1.1 points.
Versus the prior week, y/y home improvement spending growth rose the most (4.3% on Oct 31 vs 1.7% on Oct 24). Department stores slowed the most (-8.1% vs -2.2%).
Spending on holiday items was up 7.4% in the week ending Oct 31 relative to the same period 52 weeks earlier.
Lower-income households' ex-gas card spending growth has consistently outpaced higher-income households' growth over the past several weeks.
Retail ex-autos spending was up 5.0% y/y on Oct 31. Online retail rose 7.6% y/y, versus 3.7% for brick-and-mortar retail.
Airlines spending was up 7.3% y/y on Oct 31. Lodging was flat at 0.0% and restaurants and bars were up 3.0%.
Furniture (-4.1%) and department stores (-8.1%) were the weakest categories on Oct 31. Grocery was roughly flat at 0.2%.

risk_factors: The BAC data cover debit and credit cards only, exclude ACH, cash and checks, and may reflect selection bias in income levels and geographies.
Gas spending at +25% y/y inflates the headline total card growth figure.
